headline: Hurricanes place Taylor Hall on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Hurricanes have placed Taylor Hall on injured reserve, with Hall week-to-week with an upper-body injury. He has five points in eight games for Carolina.

The loss matters because Hall's start has been better than his ice time suggests. He has averaged just 13.02 minutes a game so far this season, yet his three goals sit 0.78 above what the quality of his own chances (his expected goals, 2.22) would predict. That is a modest overperformance, so some of his scoring was likely to cool anyway. The underlying play is the stronger part: Carolina has controlled 63.48% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, and the team's share of the shot quality improves by 7.41 percentage points when he plays. For a team already at 7-2-1 with 60.2% of the expected goals overall, that is a useful depth contributor to lose rather than a driver, but the Hurricanes are getting this production from a limited role. Fantasy owners should note that his scoring pace was running a little hot, and a short absence costs little in expected output.
